solution:
Write
$$\frac{2}{(x-1)(x+1)}=\frac{A}{x-1}+\frac{B}{x+1}.$$
Then $2=A(x+1)+B(x-1)$. Setting $x=1$ gives $2=2A$ so $A=1$; setting $x=-1$ gives $2=-2B$ so $B=-1$. Hence
$$\int\frac{2}{x^{2}-1}\,dx=\int\left(\frac{1}{x-1}-\frac{1}{x+1}\right)dx=\ln|x-1|-\ln|x+1|+C=\ln\left|\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right|+C.$$
hints: Find A and B by substituting convenient x-values.
Integrate each term to a logarithm.
